title: Finite D exchange stability implies strict self-consistent Voronoi
statement: For distinct positive-weight score atoms obtained by merging duplicate rows, positive-definite retained information, exactly K nonempty cells, no move constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells, and zero-tolerance exact stability, every tied-or-worse nearest-centroid comparison from a non-singleton source has strictly positive exact D gain. Stability forces distinct centroids; singleton rows are then strictly nearest to their own centroids. Hence one-point exchange stability implies strict self-consistent D-Voronoi geometry.
assumptions: coincident score rows merged, or labels constant on every duplicate class
no relocation constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells

proof_location.section: D5. Exchange stability implies strict D-Voronoi geometry

warning: The internal proof has passed the priority-0 audit. The targeted literature search found no direct equivalent, but that search gap is not a novelty/priority claim. The statement is machine-checked in Lean for arbitrary dimension d, on the merged-atoms branch of the duplicate hypothesis only; the alternative 'labels constant on every duplicate class' branch, positive gain tolerances, singular objectives, and any equivalence with the Python/JAX implementation are outside the formalization.
